subject: Recap: Discovery + next tests for Brevity Health
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Chris Johnson <chris.johnson@brevityhealth.com>, Ellie Martin <ellie@brevityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap: Discovery + next tests for Brevity Health

Hi Chris / Ellie,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the Brevity team. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get the bakeoff scheduled.

Summary of pain points you raised:
- Bursty inference spikes during chart ingestion leading to unpredictable per-token costs.
- Tail latency variability when serving longer context (clinical notes ~512–1,024 tokens).
- Data residency + HIPAA/SOC2 controls for PHI handling.
- Model hallucination risk on structured extraction tasks.

Top goals you described:
- Reduce inference cost per 1k tokens by ~30–40% versus current baseline.
- 99th percentile latency < 300 ms for 512-token workloads at typical concurrency.
- SOC2 and HIPAA-aligned deployment option (VPC/on-prem or customer-managed keys).

Proposed 48-hour bakeoff (high level):
1) Test matrix: latency (p95/p99), throughput, cost modeling (projected monthly), quality (extraction F1 / hallucination probes).
2) Variants: Redwood default model, Redwood quantized variant, CompetitorX public endpoint.
3) Infra modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (where applicable) — we’ll surface differences in data handling.
4) Deliverables: scorecard, raw traces, cost model, recommended knobs (batching/cache/quantization).

Ask from Brevity to get started:
- 3 representative prompt templates + 40 anonymized sample records we can use for quality tests (PII redaction ok).
- IT security contact to provision access or review SOC2 evidence.
- Any throughput targets or black-box test windows (preferred dates/times).

I’ve attached a short bakeoff plan that maps the tests above and the roles we’ll run on our side (redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf). If this looks good I’ll propose candidate test windows and send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Chris — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers below and a few next-step items.

1) PHI & keys: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (KMS) in Dedicated and Private deployments. For high-assurance setups we support HSM-backed policies and can include key rotation logs in the audit bundle.
2) SOC2: I’ve shared our redacted SOC2 report and supporting evidence on the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/brevity/soc2-report.pdf (link also in metadata). I can pull a shorter evidence packet (encrypted zip) for your security team — attaching security-evidence.zip.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Please upload the 3 prompt templates + 40 anonymized samples to the shared folder or send a secure SFTP link.
- Confirm a 48-hr bakeoff window from Nov 17–18 or Nov 22–23 (we can accommodate either).
- If your IT team prefers, we can run an initial proof-of-privacy test in a Dedicated environment with an HSM-backed key so they can validate logs.

If you’re good with Nov 17–18 I’ll:
- Lock a Redwood test cluster,
- Provision the dedicated namespace for the run, and
- Share the test plan checkpoints and a quick calendar invite.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Recommended test variants and gating items for Brevity bakeoff

Soojin / Karthik — quick notes from strategy:

Goals for the scorecard:
- Clear weighting between quality (F1 / hallucination rate), latency (p99), and unit cost.
- Call out operational items separately (SOC2 artifacts, PKI/HSM checks, network egress).

Must-include test variants:
- Quantized model (8-bit) vs FP16 baseline — measure quality delta and token cost improvement.
- KV/prefix caching ON vs OFF for repeated-patient prompts.
- Fallback behavior: simulate model OOM / degraded node and exercise automatic fallback to a compatible variant.

Gating / runs to request from Brevity:
- Baseline metrics from CompetitorX (short CSV of p95/p99 and average cost per million tokens if available) — ask them to share or we’ll reproduce.
- Procurement redlines early: if they have standard addenda we should get them now, run through ops & legal.

I attached a scorecard template to author during the run. Also please add HubSpot link to the RDW-2349 record and prepare DocuSign starter (we’ll only send after a positive bakeoff): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890

Thanks — keep this tight and avoid running huge parallel permutations; focus on what moves needle.

Marissa
Director, North America Sales | Redwood Inference
